amendments.rule: In a construct chain, the English relational expression belongs to the nomen rectum, headed on that noun. This is normally *of*, handled exactly as a Greek genitive `of + noun`, but where the ASV recasts the construct relation with *from*, *for*, *in*, *to*, *over*, or another preposition, that expression belongs there too. The construct state of the first noun is what signals the relation, but the first noun's unit takes only its own English word. **The rectum may be a pronominal suffix rather than a noun, and nothing changes.** Where the ASV renders such a suffix not with a possessive but with *of* and a pronoun — `כֻּלָּם` → *all of them*, `מַרְבִּיתָם` → *the greatest part of them* — the whole *of + pronoun* is the suffix's one unit, headed on the pronoun under rule 24, and the construct noun keeps only its own word: `כֹּל` takes *all*, never *all of*. Do not read that *of* as part of an English quantifier or as licensed by the construct noun's own state, for the reason this rule's third sentence gives. The corpus aligns a suffix to *of them* headed on *them* in 116 units and records no `כֹּל` → *all of* treatment, and where the construct noun's own English is something else the division shows in a single unit: `כֻּלָּם` → *five of them in all* gives *in all* to `כֹּל` and *of them* to the suffix. Where the ASV writes a possessive or a bare pronoun instead, rule 18 governs as before and there is no *of* to place. **A quantifying construct noun with a nominal rectum is read on exactly those terms.** Where `כֹּל`, `אֶחָד` or another quantifier stands in construct on a noun and the ASV writes an *of* between the two, that *of* is the chain's own relation and belongs to the rectum, the quantifier keeping only the word written for it: `אַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ` → *any* … *of thy gates* and `כָּל־עֵץ` → *any kind of tree* give *of gates* and *of tree* to their recta. **A generic noun the ASV supplies to expand the quantifier does not move that *of*.** Such a noun joins the quantifier's own unit under rule 31, which heads it on the word carrying the lexeme, so `כֹּל` takes *any kind* headed on *any*, exactly as it takes a bare *any* under rule 15 where the ASV supplies nothing. Do not read *all of*, *any of* or *any kind of* as one indivisible English quantifier: the *of* stands between the two nouns the Hebrew writes, and the subtraction test rules 16 and 31 use finds the relation between them gone when it is dropped. A partitive `מִן` before the noun is not this case, since no construct relation stands there and no morpheme but the preposition licenses either word: `מִן־הַבָּשָׂר` → *any of the flesh* is one unit on the `מִן`, headed on *any* under rule 24. **But a preposition that renders the construct noun's own lexeme is that noun's rendering and not the relation's.** Where the first noun is itself a directional or relational word and the ASV spends its one English word on that lexeme instead of writing a noun for it — `דֶּרֶךְ הַצָּפוֹן` → *toward the north*, `דֶּרֶךְ הַקָּדִים` → *toward the east* — the preposition belongs to the construct noun and heads its unit, while the rectum takes only its own word and the rectum's article takes the written *the* under rule 29. Decide it by the subtraction test rules 16, 31 and 43 use: drop the English preposition and ask whether the construct noun has lost its whole rendering or only the relation between the two nouns has gone. Where the construct noun would be left with nothing at all, the word is its own and this rule's first sentence does not reach it; where the construct noun keeps an English word of its own — `דֶּרֶךְ אַמָּה אֶחָת` → *a way of one cubit* — the first sentence stands and the *of* goes to the rectum. Do not mark such a construct `unrepresented` in order to give its preposition to the rectum: that leaves a lexical noun holding a plain English rendering unaligned, against rule 2. The corpus renders a construct `דֶּרֶךְ` by *toward*, *is toward* or *was toward* in eighteen units, always headed on the preposition, and records no unit where the rectum of such a phrase holds the preposition while the construct goes unrepresented. Two riders. Where a Hebrew preposition stands before such a construct noun and the ASV writes a single English rendering for the pair, rule 30 fuses them instead, whether that rendering is one word, as `לִפְנֵי` → *before*, or a compound preposition written in two or three, as `לְעֻמַּת` → *answerable to*, which the corpus fuses at EZK.40.18 and EZK.48.13, 18 (twice) and 21 and nowhere splits. Read rule 30's condition here as one rendering rather than one token, exactly as that rule states it: a second English word defeats the condition only where the ASV spends it on one morpheme in particular, and subtracting the *to* of *answerable to* leaves no morpheme short of a rendering of its own, since the construct noun is not a word the ASV ever writes alone; and where the phrase is the predicate of a verbless clause the construction-supplied copula joins the construct noun's unit under rule 20, as `דֶּרֶךְ הַצָּפוֹן` → *were toward the north*. **And a second `דֶּרֶךְ` standing in the same phrase is not a repetition the ASV renders once.** `הַדֶּרֶךְ דֶּרֶךְ הַצָּפוֹן` → *the way toward the north* gives *the way* to the absolute, with its article taking the *the*, and *toward* to the construct, and rule 22 reaches neither, because each has an English word of its own.
amendments.why: The rule already says the relational expression belongs to the rectum, and already forbids reading such an *of* as part of an English quantifier — but that sentence sits inside the paragraph about a pronominal suffix rectum, and DEU.16 read it as reaching no further. The chapter divided one and the same construction two ways: `אַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ` → *any of thy gates* (16.5) gave the *of* to the rectum, while `כָּל־עֵץ` → *any kind of tree* (16.21) kept *of any kind of* whole on the quantifier, on the ground that it looked like one fixed English quantifier phrase. The added passage states the same principle for a nominal rectum, settles the supplied generic (*kind*) under rule 31 rather than letting it drag the *of* with it, and marks off the partitive `מִן`, which is rule 24's and must not be harmonised with it. Nothing in the corpus contradicts it: the rule's own count records no `כֹּל` → *all of* treatment, and rule 15's `כָּל־עֵץ` → *any tree* already gives the quantifier only its own word.

conventions: A quantifying construct noun keeps only the English written for it, and the relational *of* standing between it and its rectum belongs to the rectum under rule 19: `אַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ` → *any* … *of thy gates* (16.5) and `כָּל־עֵץ` → *any kind* … *of tree* (16.21). A generic noun the ASV supplies to expand the quantifier — the *kind* of *any kind of* — joins the quantifier's own unit under rule 31 and does not move the *of*; the unit heads on the word carrying the lexeme. A partitive `מִן` is not this case: `מִן־הַבָּשָׂר` → *any of the flesh* (16.4) keeps the whole *any of* on the preposition, headed on *any* under rule 24, because no construct relation stands in the phrase.

`אֶת־פְּנֵי` before the divine name (16.16, twice) is read as the preposition H854 fused with `פָּנֶה` into the one word *before* under rule 30, headed on the construct noun, and not as an unrepresented object marker beside a noun holding the whole word. MACULA prints the class `To` for both, but glosses them *with*, where every H853 elsewhere in the chapter is glossed *(et)*; rule 16's warning against the homograph is what the division follows. Every other `אֵת` in the chapter is its own `unrepresented` unit.

`לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ` (16.2, 16.6, 16.11) divides as the written *to* on the `לְ` under rule 52 and the whole causative frame *cause … to dwell* on the Piel infinitive, headed on the complement verb *dwell* under rule 44, the unit discontinuous around the object noun. The `שָׁם` closing the clause is its own unit; at 16.6, where the ASV writes *to cause his name to dwell in, there thou shalt sacrifice*, both the stranded *in* and the fronted *there* are that one `שָׁם` realized twice under rule 25.

`עֶבֶד` → *man servant* and `אָמָה` → *maid servant* (16.11, 16.14) both head on *servant*, reading *man* and *maid* as the ASV's specifiers under rule 31's tie-break, since *servant* is a noun the ASV writes alone for a word of that class. Heading each on the specifier is the defensible alternative and is named in both verses' notes. The chapter's other supplied-generic phrases go the other way on the same test, because the ASV never writes the generic alone for those words: `חָמֵץ` → *leavened bread*, `מַצּוֹת` → *unleavened bread*, `קָמָה` → *standing grain*, `גֹּרֶן` → *threshing floor*, `נְדָבָה` → *freewill offering* all head on the modifier.

report: One genuine cross-verse split: a quantifying construct noun and its rectum are divided two ways. DEU.16.5 gives `אַחַד` only its own *any* and the relational *of* to the rectum (`שְׁעָרֶיךָ` → *of ... gates*), which is rule 19's first sentence together with its `כֹּל` takes *all*, never *all of* ruling; DEU.16.21 kept the whole *of any kind of* on `כָּל` and left `עֵץ` a bare *tree*. Nothing in the source licenses the difference — both are a construct quantifier over a noun with an *of* written between the two — so DEU.16.21 is patched to match.

The patch moves only the second *of* (t011). The leading *of* (t008) stays with `כֹּל`: it introduces the whole appositional phrase `כָּל־עֵץ` standing after `אֲשֵׁרָה`, and is rule 33's supplied preposition, which goes to the word opening that phrase. The supplied generic *kind* stays with `כֹּל` under rule 31, and the unit still heads on *any*.

Checked and deliberately left alone: DEU.16.4's partitive `מִן־הַבָּשָׂר` → *any of the flesh* keeps *any of* whole on the preposition. No construct relation stands there and nothing but the `מִן` licenses either word, so rule 24 governs and rule 19 does not reach it. A later reader should not harmonise it with 16.21.

The other candidate groups are the ASV rendering one word differently, or the source differing: `לֹא` *no* vs *not* (determiner recasting vs plain negation); `הַ` aligned vs unrepresented (a written *the* against *a year*, *a bribe*, an agreement article on an ordinal, and the demonstrative taking the phrase's one determiner at 16.12); `בְּ` *in*/*at*/*on*/*to*/*within*, including the 16.4 pair where `בָּעֶרֶב` loses its article and `בַּיּוֹם` loses its preposition; `לְ` with a written *to*/*unto* against the unrepresented ethical datives and the bare modal complement at 16.5; `חַג` and `פֶּסַח`, where the single *the* goes to a present article morpheme when there is one and to the construct when there is not; `יָצָא` at 16.3 and 16.6, both giving the construct relation's *when*/*that* to the infinitive; `שָׁם` at 16.6 realised twice under rule 25. None is a split.

The table is blind to `added` units, so the five were read end to end against the verses that fold a comparable word in: *even* (16.3), *it* (16.7), italic *therein* (16.8), *to put* (16.9) and *shall give* (16.17). Each stands beside a clause where no morpheme is present to carry it, and no other verse folds the same kind of word into a neighbour. Consistent.

BSB disagreements are all documented convention differences, and none is a genuine error. The 5 `Td` and 11 `R` cases are articles and prepositions the ASV's recasting leaves without an English word (rules 29, 40, 52); 16.7's `וֹ` and 16.13's `ךָ` are a resumptive and an ethical-dative suffix the ASV writes nothing for (rules 22, 40); 16.4's `בַּ` is the `בַּיּוֹם` of *the first day*, where the phrase's one English function word is the *the* rule 47 gives the article. BSB attaches each to its host phrase, which is its stated convention. No accepted edge was changed to improve the rate.

Four conventions recorded, since the report shows 63 notes repeating across verses with nothing in the log. One amendment to rule 19, widening its existing `כֹּל` takes *all*, never *all of* ruling from a pronominal rectum to a nominal one, which is the sentence this chapter needed and did not have.
